messages:
olivia (support): Customer escalated: their service started getting 404s fetching our Go SDK after upgrading to our v2 tag. They say `go get` fails in CI and their deploys are blocked. They provided a minimal repro and a go.mod. Asking for an urgent workaround and whether we should retag.

sam (eng): Can you paste the exact `go get` error and the go.mod they used? 404 from proxy or from GitHub? Any private replace directives?

olivia (support): Error snippet from CI: 
```
go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0: reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/@v/v2.0.0.info: 404 Not Found
go: error loading module requirements
```
Their go.mod (sanitized):
```
module example.com/customer

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
)
```
No `replace` in their top-level go.mod. They say `go env GOPROXY` is default and they can't `go get` the tag.

junaid (eng-runtime): Quick suspicion: module path vs tagged release mismatch. If the module in the repo is still declared as `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` (no `/v2`), then v2 tags will be treated as a v2 module and `go` expects the path to include `/v2`. If tag exists but module path is wrong, some proxies return 404. Could also be GOPRIVATE/GOPROXY interplay.

sam (eng): Ask customer to `git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk.git` and confirm tag exists. Also ask them to run `GOPROXY=direct GOPRIVATE= github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0` to see if proxy is the block.

marie (cs): Customer says the tag is there and public. They also mentioned they tried `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0` and saw the same 404. They reported the upgrade started yesterday after we published v2.0.0.

olivia (support): I pulled the repo at the tag and inspected go.mod in the tag: it has `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk`. So yes — tag mismatch. That explains proxy 404s.

deploy-bot: Release pipeline failed for tag v2.0.0 -> job 'verify-module-path' exited non-zero. See CI run https://ci.internal/redwood/releases/9876 : :warning:

junaid (eng-runtime): We should fix this ASAP. Options: 1) Create a v2.0.1 tag where the checked-out go.mod has `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` (recommended). 2) If we can't retag, instruct customers to add a temporary `replace` to point to a commit: `replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v0.0.0-<commit>` which is messy. 3) Ask customers to set `GOPRIVATE`/GOPROXY adjustments (only works if proxy is the blocker).

sam (eng): For quick mitigation, create a short-lived v2.0.1 release that fixes module path. Also add a release note and pin in our release docs explaining what happened and the fix. I'll take the tag. @deploy-bot can you open a release task and schedule a retag?

deploy-bot: Created release task RED-REL-3123 and queued retag job.

marie (cs): I'll tell the customer the plan: we'll publish v2.0.1 with corrected module path and provide a temporary workaround: add this to their go.mod to unblock CI: `replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v0.0.0-2021948523-abcdef123456` (use commit sha we give them). Also recommend clearing proxy cache if they still see 404.

olivia (support): One more note from the customer: their service retried failed `go get` in CI loops and it blew their CI minutes / billing. They're asking if we can invalidate proxy entry so `go` failures return fast instead of retrying.

junaid (eng-runtime): We can't change third-party proxy behavior, but we can expedite the fixed tag. Also suggest they add exponential backoff in their CI step or a short `sleep` between retries to avoid billing spikes. We'll prioritize the retag and flag REL-3123 as P0.

sam (eng): I'll also add a small CI check to our release pipeline to verify `module` path in the published tag matches expected `/vN` suffix for major>v1. Prevents recurrence.

marie (cs): Customer ok with plan. They'll wait for v2.0.1 and want a heads up once published.

olivia (support): Thanks — marking as escalated and tracking RED-REL-3123. I'll DM the customer once the fixed tag is live. :white_check_mark:
